title: Cohort Onboarding & Role Activation Manual
author: Aisha R. Patel
body:
Overview

This manual defines Redwood's cohort-based onboarding approach and the complementary role-activation process that ensures new contributors have the correct privileges, expectations, and growth touchpoints. It consolidates: working-at-Redwood orientation, role ladder activation, benefits signposting, hiring manager responsibilities, and the internal tools access matrix used by IT and People Ops.

Audience
- New joiners across engineering, product, and GTM functions joining cohort onboarding.
- Hiring managers, onboarding buddies, people-ops partners, and IT provisioning engineers.

Goals
- Provide a repeatable cohort experience that accelerates productive contribution within 30 days.
- Ensure role ladders and compensation/benefits visibility are clear by day 15.
- Prevent over- and under-provisioning by standardizing tool access per role and employment type.

Scope and exclusions
- Applies to full-time employees and long-term contractors (>6 months). Short-term contractors, interns, and externals follow the separate contractor onboarding matrix (see related pages).
- Does not replace role-specific technical onboarding delivered by teams (e.g., runtime onboarding, security orientation).

Cohort model (high level)
1. Cohort cadence: new cohorts start every Monday. For hires who join mid-week, assign them to the next cohort or run one-off expedited onboarding (manager decision).
2. Cohort size target: 6–20 contributors per cohort for best interaction.
3. Duration: 4-week orchestrated program with optional 8-week technical deep-dive tracks.
4. Delivery: blended — live orientation sessions (Zoom), recorded modules (LMS), and team-run role shadowing.

Week-by-week cohort outline
- Week 0 (Pre-boarding) — before start date:
  - HR sends employment packet and benefits portal link.
  - IT creates staged accounts in the provisioning queue and sends the new-joiner hardware survey.
  - People Ops assigns cohort number and Slack cohort channel (#cohort-YYMMDD).

- Week 1 — Foundations:
  - Day 1: Welcome session (People Ops) — company mission, values, benefits overview, basic security.
  - Day 2: Manager meeting — role context, 30/60/90 expectations.
  - Day 3: Tools orientation — GitHub, Jira, CI previews, and Redwood Console walkthrough.
  - End of week: Buddy check-in and first-week feedback form.

- Week 2 — Role and Team Integration:
  - Team-specific tech onboarding (data access requests if needed).
  - Role ladder & compensation Q&A (People Ops optional drop-in).
  - Shadowing and pairing assignments begin.

- Week 3 — Execution:
  - First small delivery (bug fix, doc contribution, simple eval).
  - Career conversation with manager to align ladders and growth goals.

- Week 4 — Calibration and Transition:
  - 30-day manager review (documented in People Ops system).
  - Add to continuous learning pathway and schedule 90-day checkpoints.

Role ladder activation process (step-by-step)
1. Role definition and offer: Recruiter confirms level (e.g., IC2, IC3, Manager1) in offer.
2. People Ops creates a role-activation record in HRIS with the level, base comp, and expected promotion horizon.
3. Manager and new hire complete the "Role Expectation Form" by day 7.
4. People Ops schedules a role-ladder orientation slot in week 2.
5. At day 30, manager records initial calibration: confirming level/expectations and scheduling a development plan if needed.

Hiring manager checklist (minimum responsibilities)
- Pre-boarding: confirm equipment and run a short team welcome note.
- Day 1: meet & set 30/60/90 goals in writing.
- Week 2: schedule role ladder Q&A and identify the first pairing partner.
- Day 30: complete the 30-day review and update People Ops.
- Day 90: deliver a competence calibration and identify promotion blockers or support needs.

Internal tools access matrix (standardized defaults)
Note: IT/Provisioning uses this table as the baseline. All requests that deviate must include manager approval and use the Access Exception form.

| System | Full-time Engineer | Product Manager | People Ops | Contractor (long-term) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| GitHub (org) | write | write | read | write (limited repos) | Engineers get main repo access by default; contractors restricted to a single repo set. |
| Jira (standard) | write | write | admin | write | Product & Eng: access to private product boards; People Ops limited admin for HR-related projects. |
| Redwood Console (prod) | read | read | read | no | Prod write access requires SRE sign-off and approved RBAC ticket. |
| Internal Wiki | write | write | write | read | Editing rights for full-time staff. |
| Payroll/Benefits Portal | no | no | admin | no | People Ops handles benefits enrollment. |
| AWS Console (prod) | no | no | no | no | Accessed via bastion and approved requests; separate infra process. |

Provisioning SLA and ownership
- Target SLA for baseline provisioning (accounts, laptop, Slack): 5 business days before start date. For late hires this becomes 2 business days after request.
- IT Provisioning team owner: it-provisioning@redwood.internal (SLA owner).
- Escalation: if provisioning misses SLA, hiring manager escalates to People Ops partner and the onboarding program lead.

Benefits and perks signposting (what to expect in week 0–2)
- Benefits enrollment window opens on Day 1 and remains for 30 days. People Ops sends reminders on days 3, 10, and 20.
- Stipends (home-office, learning): auto-eligible after payroll activation; request through internal finance form.
- Parental and caregiver policies summarized with links in the LMS module.

Special cases and exceptions
- Remote-first hires across APAC/EU: tax and benefits packaging will differ; People Ops will provide a jurisdiction-specific packet within 48 hours of start.
- Senior hires (Director and above): many provisioning steps are manual (exec laptop prep, additional security briefings) — onboarding lead will create a bespoke checklist.

Onboarding feedback and metrics (how we measure success)
- Primary metrics: time-to-first-PR, 30-day self-reported readiness, manager 30-day rating (1–5).
- Target goals: 75% of cohorts hit time-to-first-PR within 21 days; average manager 30-day rating >= 4.0.
- Monthly retrospective: People Ops runs a 60-minute cohort retro and submits a short improvement plan.

Security & compliance requirements during onboarding
- All new joiners must complete the Secure SDL course within 7 days.
- MFA must be enabled on all accounts before any write-level repo access is granted.
- Contractors must sign the Contractor Data Protection Addendum before being granted access to internal datasets.

Templates and artifacts (quick links)
- Role Expectation Form (Template): /templates/role-expectation-form.docx
- Access Exception Form: /forms/access-exception.pdf
- Cohort feedback survey (LMS): /lms/cohort-feedback
- First-30 Review form (People Ops system): /people-ops/30-day-review

Appendix: Example CLI snippet for IT provisioning (for provisioning automation engineers)

# Example: create baseline GitHub team and invite user (placeholder script)
# Note: this is an illustrative snippet; production automation runs in the provisioning service.

curl -X POST https://api.github.com/orgs/redwood/teams \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"name":"eng-new-joiners-202603","privacy":"closed"}'

curl -X PUT https://api.github.com/orgs/redwood/teams/eng-new-joiners-202603/memberships/{username} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"role":"member"}'

Ownership and contact points
- Program owner: People Ops Onboarding Squad (onboarding@redwood.internal).
- IT provisioning: it-provisioning@redwood.internal.
- Escalation: people-ops-lead@redwood.internal, vp-people@redwood.internal.
